transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

The '4C' code on Samsung dishwashers typically indicates a water supply issue – meaning the machine isn't getting enough fresh water to start. This is often caused by the tap being off, the inlet hose being kinked behind the machine, or the small filter at the connection point being blocked. Please check two things: 1. Is the hot or cold water tap behind the dishwasher fully turned on? 2. Look at the flexible inlet hose going into the back of the machine – is it kinked, squashed or bent sharply? Let me know what you find.

There's no tap behind it, just a screwdriver-slot valve under the sink, and it's turned so the slot is at 90 degrees to the pipe. The hose has no kinks. A plumber fitted a new kitchen tap yesterday and it's done this since.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The '4C' code suggests the dishwasher isn't getting enough water. Since a plumber just fitted a new tap, it is very likely that debris (like tape, sealant or grit) has entered the system and blocked the small mesh filter inside the dishwasher's inlet connection, or that the under-sink valve isn't fully open. Please check two things:
1. Is the screwdriver-slot valve under the sink turned so the slot is parallel to the pipe (fully open)? If it's at 90 degrees, it might be closed or only half-open.
2. Turn off the water supply, unscrew the inlet hose from the back of the dishwasher, and look inside the small mesh filter in the machine's inlet port. Is there grit or debris blocking it? Let me know what you find.
I turned the valve so the slot runs along the pipe and started it again. It's filling now and running normally. I haven't taken the hose off to look at the filter.

That's excellent news – it sounds like the plumber had left that under-sink valve slightly closed or partially obstructed by debris from the new tap installation. Since it is filling and running normally now, you have successfully resolved the 4C error code. As a quick tip for next time: always ensure those screwdriver-slot valves are turned so the slot runs parallel to the pipe (fully open) when installing or moving appliances. If this happens again, checking that valve position first is usually the fastest fix before worrying about filters or hoses. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
